title: C415 — Right-hand rear lamp assembly connector
introduction:
The right-hand rear lamp connector is a small junction with several different duties. I read its table like a theater cue sheet: park, turn and stop labels tell you which job a connection belongs to, but they do not prove the lamp received its cue or performed it.

Check the identification table, locate a cavity label in the drawing and follow its matching Cavity row across the circuit table. Keep the circuit identifier, color, gauge and full function together. In particular, retain the left-side wording in the signal-out and ground descriptions even though the assembly title identifies the right-hand lamp. Those labels do not establish the wiring route. Use the final table to cross-reference the listed pigtail service item.

This page establishes reference relationships, not access, connector release, live probing or replacement steps. Physical viewing direction, the gauge convention and the meanings of Size and Used are not defined here. Keep those entries unchanged and obtain the matching service information before attempting work beyond reading the reference.

edits.why: I orient the drawing on the page by its broad left projection and hooked lower-right outline. The labeled cavities occupy aligned columns, with the lower-left position shaded. That shading corresponds to the row without a circuit or function assignment. It helps explain the drawing’s relationship to the table; it does not establish a physical viewing side or a connector release motion.

Each Cavity row links a drawn position to its circuit description and wire details. The park, turn, ground, signal-out and stop labels describe different roles, so read the full function rather than choosing by a familiar color. Preserve the left-side descriptions within this right-hand assembly reference. I do not reinterpret those labels as a routing diagram, and the blank assignment row remains blank.

A pigtail combines a connector with attached wire leads. Kit List and Number connect the identification and service-parts tables; Hard Shell and Engineering Shell provide another comparison. Keep the service-item reference separate from the individual Terminal Part Number entries. Its listed Gauge is not an instruction to make every circuit wire the same size, and the table supplies no replacement or splicing sequence.
